blackrhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf seen from a THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE, its head turned toward the viewer and its body angled away so both the face and one full flank show. Only a few months old, with unmistakably infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded body, a soft rounded forehead and big soft eyes. ON TOP OF ITS NOSE SITS ONE SMALL SOFT ROUNDED GREY KNOB, a low blunt bump about the size of its own eye, smooth and pebble-shaped and barely raised above the skin, like a small river stone resting on a table - this little pebble-bump is the only thing on its nose and it is tiny, rounded and stubby, never tall, never pointed, never a spike. Below it a POINTED HOOKED PREHENSILE UPPER LIP for browsing. Soft mid-grey skin, evenly lit, small tubular ears, a stubby tail
baskingshark: An enormous gentle plankton-straining sea creature seen in side profile, swimming slowly forward with its jaws opened to their fullest extent. ITS OWN HEAD IS THE OPENING: its jaws are hinged far back near its gills and swing open so enormously wide that the front third of the animal's body becomes one great round hollow funnel, a barrel-shaped cavern carved straight out of the head itself, with its small dark eye sitting on the outside of that funnel just behind the corner of the jaw. The mouth is not a separate ring or hoop in front of it, and there is no loose hoop or floating circle anywhere - the opening IS the front of its head, continuous with its body, its own upper jaw forming the roof and its own lower jaw the floor. Lining the inside walls of that funnel, and only on the inside, is a soft pale fringe of fine flexible hair-like combs. The outer rim where the jaws meet the face is smooth, plain, bare and even all the way round. Behind the funnel, five colossal gill slits encircle the head, meeting over the top of the back and beneath the throat like stacked collars. A bulky heavy grey-brown body, a tall triangular fin on its back, a crescent tail. Slow, harmless and gentle
sunfishmola: A giant ocean sunfish SEEN IN STRICT SIDE PROFILE, side-on to the viewer and swimming from left to right, showing its whole flank flat to us with ONE eye on the side of its head and its small round mouth pointing left toward the front. ITS BODY IS AN ENORMOUS FLAT ROUND SILVER PLATE STANDING ON EDGE - a full moon, a dinner plate, a car wheel - exactly as tall from back to belly as it is long from face to rear, squashed flat from side to side like a coin. THE REAR OF THIS DISC IS COMPLETELY MISSING, as though the whole back half had been SLICED CLEAN OFF WITH A KNIFE straight down: the body simply ENDS in a blunt vertical cut edge trimmed with a short WAVY SCALLOPED FRILL OF SKIN lying flush against that cut like a pie crust, no longer than a hand. NOTHING ELSE PROJECTS FROM THE BACK OR THE UNDERSIDE - no tail, no fan, no fork, no trailing fin of any kind below or behind. From the TOP of the circle ONE ENORMOUS POINTED FIN rises straight UP and from the BOTTOM one identical fin points straight DOWN, and those two are the only large fins on the animal. A tiny round mouth, one large round eye, small pectoral fins, rough mottled silver-grey hide
